sections.overview: Ammobatoides abdominalis is a solitary cuckoo bee in the family Apidae. It is a brood parasite of other bees rather than a pollen-collecting nest builder.
sections.identification: Adults are about 10–12 mm long; no dependable height, body width or mass figures were found. Females have red front abdominal segments and hind legs against a mostly black body, while males are black with conspicuously large eyes and pale hair bands; these contrasting patterns make the sexes recognizable in the field.
sections.habitat: The species is recorded across much of central and eastern Europe and western to central Asia, reaching Xinjiang in China.
sections.diet: Adults visit flowers for nectar; records include thyme, white sweet-clover and knapweeds, among other plants.
sections.behavior: Both sexes have been observed gripping grass stems or similar supports with their mandibles while sleeping.
sections.reproduction: The female lays in nests of Melitturga bees; Melitturga clavicornis is recorded as the host in central Europe, and other Melitturga species are reported elsewhere in its range. The exact egg-laying behavior is unknown.
sections.ecology: The species has one generation each year and is active in summer, with adults generally flying from June into August.
sections.conservation: The European Red List classifies it as Endangered (EN) in Europe and the EU 27. Germany lists it as extinct or lost, with the last documented observation in 1959; this is a national status and does not mean the species is globally extinct.
